picked.title: WEVO: World Model-Enabled VLA Optimization for Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation
picked.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve vision-language-action (VLA) policies beyond imitation, but humanoid exploration is unsafe and simulator RL can exploit residual sim-to-real gaps. We present WEVO, a teleoperation-free framework for post-training a whole-body humanoid VLA in an action-conditioned video world model (WM). Simulated manipulation and locomotion play data improve contact-dynamics and viewpoint-change prediction. A VLA trained on synthetic demonstrations collects 20 autonomous real robot rollouts per task to align the WM with deployment observations. The VLA, whole-body controller (WBC), and video WM then form a closed-loop RL environment with dense progress rewards. Across three real robot tasks, play data improves every evaluated WM metric and downstream policy success; video WM RL raises mean success from 23.3% to 75.0%, compared with 48.3% for real robot RL. We therefore leverage the complementary strengths of both environments: simulation provides policy initialization and broad coverage, while the video WM offers a deployment-aligned environment for policy improvement. Project website: https://qianzhong-chen.github.io/wevo.github.io/.

picked.title: One View, One Action: Spatially Generalizable VLAs through Observation-Aligned Experts and Cross Graph Consistency
picked.summary: Multi-view vision-language-action (VLA) models still face challenges in spatial generalization, particularly under changes in camera viewpoints and robot initial states. These models typically receive action supervision only in the robot base frame, requiring them to implicitly learn the spatial correspondence between observations from each view and base-frame actions. We propose One View, One Action (OVOA-VLA), which learns to predict actions in each view's camera frame, allowing the same physical motion to provide diverse, observation-aligned supervision across views. OVOA-VLA jointly trains a base-frame expert and view-specific action experts, whose robot-state inputs and action targets are expressed in their respective camera frames. Two complementary directed attention graphs model both directions of interaction between the base and view-specific experts, jointly leveraging view-specific action supervision to improve base-frame prediction. Cross Graph Consistency further encourages agreement between the two graphs' base-frame predictions for the same sample. With the same multi-view inputs, the model supports both full and base-only inference. Experiments across multiple simulation benchmarks demonstrate improved manipulation performance and robustness to camera-viewpoint and robot-initialization perturbations. Full and base-only inference achieve average success rates of 88.1% and 85.7% on LIBERO-Plus, respectively. In real-world evaluations, base-only inference raises the average success rates from $π_{0.5}$'s 28.3% to 58.3% across three tasks under spatial distribution shifts.

picked.title: Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
picked.summary: Large multimodal models can support long-horizon robot manipulation, but frequent model calls incur substantial latency and token costs. The central challenge is determining when agent assistance or intervention is needed and whether errors require correcting robot execution, subtask planning, or both. To address this problem, we propose RoC (Reasoning on Call), an efficient framework that coordinates a low-level policy and a high-level reasoning agent through an online task-state monitor. The monitor combines temporal visual observations with ordered interaction memory to jointly estimate progress within the active subtask and predict its successor. These predictions guide event-triggered agent review for coordinated execution repair and plan revision. Verified outcomes govern memory updates and subtask transitions, allowing routine execution to remain with the policy while reasoning focuses on decisions requiring additional assessment. On RMBench, RoC improves task success rate by 24.0 percentage points and reduces token consumption by 65.3% compared with the strongest agent-based baseline. It also outperforms the strongest policy-based baseline by 15.1 percentage points in task success rate. Real-world experiments further validate its effectiveness across three long-horizon manipulation tasks. Overall, RoC supports efficient agent intervention and coordinated recovery across execution and planning for long-horizon robot manipulation.

picked.title: CauSyncVLA: Causal Latent World Modeling for Asynchronous Robot Control
picked.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies must react while visual inference is still running. Overlapping computation and execution reduces waiting, yet leaves perceptual memory stale and successive action chunks disconnected. We present CauSyncVLA, an asynchronous dual-system controller that aligns perceptual-memory prediction and trajectory correction with actual robot execution. Rather than forecasting pixels or physical states, a Causal Latent World Model predicts current perceptual memory from delayed visual anchors and executed state-action history, supervised through action-sensitive distillation to retain the frozen expert's control response. Conditioned on this updated memory, Predictive Flow Warm-Starting (PFWS) aligns the unexecuted action horizon for single-step flow correction without extra training. On LIBERO-10, CauSyncVLA reaches 93.8% success at 5.04$\times$ inference throughput, improving closed-loop robustness and robot motion smoothness.

picked.title: Video Friday: Drone Squeezes Itself to Fit Through Tight Spaces
picked.summary: Drones navigating cluttered spaces often encounter openings narrower than their bodies. We present a design method that jointly optimizes a quadrotor’s geometry and how its two side arms bend on contact. The resulting prototype folds from 31.3 cm to 14.1 cm wide on contact and flies through a 15 cm opening. [ Paper ] via [ Autonomous Robots Lab ] Thanks, Kostas! TeCoBots are soft, snake-like robots that can work alone and can also grab onto each other to form chains, loops and branches, building a new body for each task. A single robot can inch like a worm, roll across gravel and grass, climb inside a pipe and lift a 2.5-liter water bottle. The claw it uses to grab objects is the same one it uses to grab another robot, so linking up needs no extra docking hardware. Linked together, the robots do things none can do alone. [ TeCoBots ] Thanks, Mahmud! AHEADance is a humanoid robot that makes up its dance as the music plays. It listens to the song as it streams in, takes a guess at what the next half second of music will sound like, and moves to match, in the style of whatever is playing. When the music stops, it stands still and waits, and when the music comes back, so does the dancing. Curious what it would do with your favourite song? Play it through the live demo on our project page and watch the robot have a go. [ AHEADance ] Thanks, Chengxu! I am... Not at all sure how I feel about this. picked.title: 方程豹钛9上市：27.99万元起，折叠方向盘首次上车
picked.summary: 11月19日，方程豹钛9正式上市，售价27.99万元起，置换价27.39万元起。作为比亚迪2026年收官车型，钛9首搭折叠智舱及DMS超级混动全能平台，进一步进入大型六座SUV市场。 雷峰网了解到，折叠智舱搭载于钛9顶配版本，将折叠方向盘、躺平座椅、线控数字底盘与智慧生态结合。与常见的座椅放倒休息不同，这套方案将方向盘一并收纳，为驾驶位释放更多空间。 方程豹将钛9的产品主张概括为“定义全维硬派新境”。从此次发布的配置来看，它既保留了方盒子造型和全地形能力，也将空间、座舱和六座舒适性作为重点，希望覆盖家庭出行、长途自驾与户外活动等需求。 折叠方向盘上车，驾驶位可以怎样变？ 钛9此次最受关注的配置，是顶配版本搭载的折叠方向盘。 按照官方介绍，这套方向盘支持0°至180°折叠，收纳过程控制在10秒以内，启停耐久寿命可达8万次。在离车泊入、泊出过程中，方向盘还可以同步完成折叠或展开。 与之配合的是可一键躺平的驾驶位座椅。座椅支持18向调节，靠背最大躺角165°，腿部最大膝角157°，约20秒完成躺平，无需拆卸头枕或下车调整。 方向盘收纳之后，驾驶位的休息空间得以扩大。对需要在车内午休，或在长途补能时短暂休息的用户来说，这是一项比较直接的用途。 比亚迪表示，折叠智舱也是其面向L3、L4级智能驾驶的技术储备。需要区分的是，座舱硬件的量产，并不等同于车辆已经具备相应等级的自动驾驶能力。 …
